note: Divergences between the committed Cloud Armor capture and what edge.ts declares that are known and recorded. The GCP edge is being wound down, so closing them means changing a deployed policy on its way out, which is a deliberate decision rather than routine remediation. Read alongside CLOUD-ARMOR-BASELINE.md's 'Machine-checked parity' section, which explains why they are recorded rather than left as a permanently red check. Each entry matches one priority, one field and one exact observed value: there is no wildcard form, so an entry cannot grow to cover a divergence nobody decided to accept. An entry whose divergence stops happening fails the check until it is deleted, so this list shrinks visibly as remediation lands and never silently re-accepts a fixed problem.

accepted.reason: The captured sqli rule carries preview: it records a match rather than acting on it, while edge.ts declares the rule enforcing. See CLOUD-ARMOR-BASELINE.md, 'The capture and the code diverge on eight fields'.
accepted.closedBy: A deliberate change against the deployed policy, then re-running the capture procedure in CLOUD-ARMOR-BASELINE.md and deleting this entry in the same commit as the fresh capture. Superseded outright if the GCP edge is retired first.

accepted.reason: The captured policy carries the preview-mode sqli-v33-stable rule for the preview-only-host carve-out, scoped to blog.branchleft.co.uk. edge.ts no longer declares it: that tenant was re-provisioned on Hetzner on 2026-09-10 and its sites.ts entry lost its cloudRunService, and edge.ts builds previewOnlyHosts only from sites this edge actually serves. blog was the last such host, so the whole 1100+ family is now undeclared while remaining live. Safe to hold: the rule is preview: true, so it records a match rather than acting on one, and its expression matches only that one Host -- neither condition lets it override another rule's enforcement, which is the risk the undeclared-rule check exists to raise.
accepted.closedBy: Applying edge.ts's current shape to the deployed policy, which removes this rule, then re-running the capture procedure in CLOUD-ARMOR-BASELINE.md and deleting this entry in the same commit as the fresh capture. Superseded outright if the GCP edge is retired first, which is now the likelier order.
